expectation: corporate power is a live lexical register, not a name
rationale: The genre's founding triangle (Gibson's zaibatsu worlds, Stephenson's franchulate, Sterling's Movement) makes the firm the ambient institution, so corporate vocabulary should be ordinary texture, not a single proper noun.
falsifier: corporate density at generic-prose level would strip the prediction: the corporation is named but not rendered.

expectation: a dense digital/technological register carries the texture
rationale: Cyberpunk's surface is made of interfaces, data flows and electronics; the register should be dense and it should be neologism-prone, since the genre coins its own hardware words.
falsifier: a digital register no denser than prose would mean the technology is named, not inhabited.

expectation: body and machine fuse inside single clauses, not across them
rationale: The cyborg is the genre's body: interface as tissue, so machine and body vocabulary should share clauses more than chance allows.
falsifier: machine and organ vocabulary in separate clauses would be adjacency, not fusion.

expectation: the dystopia is named in a proper-noun layer
rationale: Genre worlds are named (the Sprawl, Neo-Tokyo, the zaibatsu); the book's own jacket names Sato Corporation, Cadaver City and Placenta World, and #59 tested those names against the text.
falsifier: if the named place/organization entities were refuted against the text, the proper-noun layer would be marketing only.

expectation: metal is a live material register of the body
rationale: Tsukamoto's Metal Fetishist assimilates iron and scrap into flesh; the prior expects metal words to be ordinary material vocabulary, not a rare image.
falsifier: metal at generic-prose density would mean the fusion is organic-only: the machine-horror is metaphoric.

expectation: transformation is processual: mutation and proliferation verbs
rationale: The film's horror is *becoming* -- liquefaction, fusion, excrescence -- so the process verbs should be a live class.
falsifier: a transformation register at prose density would reduce the body-horror to static description.

expectation: fusion happens in contact: metal and organ in the same clause
rationale: The prior image is metal *inside* the body, so the two registers should co-occur within clauses beyond chance.
falsifier: metal and organ vocabulary never sharing a clause would mean no fusion is ever staged.

expectation: the horror is located in the body's interior
rationale: Body horror's camera looks inward: organs, entrails, flesh as the stage of the event.
falsifier: an organ register at prose density would locate the horror outside the body.

expectation: a clinical register is over-dense against ordinary prose
rationale: Ballard's diction is medicine-show: syndromes, sera, inoculations, pathologies as ordinary words, so the clinical register should stand far above prose.
falsifier: clinical at prose density would remove Ballard's method rather than his themes.

expectation: the affect profile is the new psychopathology
rationale: 'Inner space' Ballard expects fear, ecstasy, paranoia and disgust to be *elevated together* -- the pathology is euphoric, not merely dreadful.
falsifier: an affect profile flat against the English baseline would make the book's affect ordinary.

expectation: violence is eroticized: sex and violence share clauses
rationale: Crash's scandal is the erotic charge of the collision; the prior expects sexual and violent vocabulary fused at clause level.
falsifier: sexual and violent registers in separate clauses would be Ballard's subject matter without Ballard's fusion.

expectation: the pathology is organized as a case with testable claims
rationale: Even at their most deranged, Ballard's texts keep a clinical scaffolding: named subjects doing definable things to definable targets, whose claims can be checked and can fail.
falsifier: if the event layer were dense while every named predicate were refuted, there would be no case, only texture.

expectation: reproduction is a live and distinctive register
rationale: Berg's 'mommy trilogy' makes pregnancy, birth and the genetic a central grotesque; the prior expects the reproductive lexicon to be unusually dense.
falsifier: reproduction at prose density would make the fertility imagery incidental.

expectation: the grotesque is a named register, not an accident
rationale: The criticism of Berg describes a violently grotesque register; the prior expects a deformation vocabulary standing well above prose.
falsifier: grotesque at prose density would make the deformation rhetorical rather than systemic.

expectation: birth and grotesque fuse in single clauses
rationale: In Berg the birth event *is* the deformation event, so the two registers should share clauses beyond chance.
falsifier: the two registers in separate clauses would separate birth from horror, which is not the prior's image.

expectation: tenderness persists inside the grotesque
rationale: Berg's signature is horror blended with empathy -- the grotesque body is also loved -- so the prior expects tender wording inside the deformation register.
falsifier: unmeasurable here: no workspace lexicon separates tenderness from ecstasy (see the annotation).

expectation: syntax is deranged but not noise
rationale: Butler's prose deranges syntax while remaining predictable-ish above chance; the prior expects parseability below ordinary English yet above a shuffle null.
falsifier: parseability at prose level would be ordinary syntax; at null level would be noise rather than a system.

expectation: phrases recur densely enough to be formulas
rationale: Butler's roiling repetition: the same phrases churn, so a large share of the text should sit in repeated n-grams.
falsifier: a text with no recurring phrase skeleton would be all novelty, no pressure.

expectation: the book loops back on itself
rationale: Butler's copycat structures and obsessive returns expect long-range self-similarity, not local coherence.
falsifier: self-similarity at chance level would remove the loop structure the prior expects.

expectation: narrative time is elliptical
rationale: Butler's narratives refuse chronology; the prior expects no recoverable temporal order of events.
falsifier: unmeasurable here: no workspace artifact measures temporal order (see the annotation).

expectation: the surface is code-like: operators as a structural share
rationale: Codework's poetics is the executable surface -- punctuation as syntax, operators as grammar -- so operator density should be a structural fraction, not ornament.
falsifier: operators at ornament level would make the surface look code-like without being code-like.

expectation: infection is a live and distinctive register
rationale: The text-virus prior takes infection literally: virus, infection, parasite as the genre's governing metaphor made of words.
falsifier: infection at prose density would leave the virus as a title only.

expectation: the virus is digital: infection and technology share clauses
rationale: In codework the virus is *code* -- the biological and the computational are one figure -- so the registers should be fused at clause level.
falsifier: the two registers in separate clauses would keep the virus biological and the data merely technical.

expectation: an asemic layer: invented surfaces outside the dictionary
rationale: Codework and asemic writing expect machine-coined, non-dictionary surfaces as a visible layer of the text.
falsifier: no true-coinage layer would make the invention decorative rather than systemic.

expectation: a command/scream layer in capitals
rationale: Codework's machine voice shouts in caps -- commands, labels, LOAD -- so an ALL-CAPS functional layer should be measurable.
falsifier: no caps layer would leave the machine voice unwritten.
